reason: E2 shows structural stability and no segregation in Ru-5 MEA-NPs up to 873 K, and E3 links entropy to sluggish kinetics and uniform distribution at 773 K via simulation, supporting the diffusion-barrier premise. However, neither E2 nor E3 provides evidence for stability up to 1923 K, for the specific magnitude of diffusion reduction relative to binary alloys, or for the direct causal chain from configurational entropy to lattice distortion to increased diffusion barriers; these key premises remain unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: High configurational entropy increases lattice distortion in multi-element nanoparticles
Increased lattice distortion raises the activation energy for atomic diffusion
Sluggish diffusion kinetics prevent elemental segregation and phase separation at high temperatures
Quinary nanoparticles can retain a homogeneous solid solution up to 1923 K under inert conditions
Diffusion coefficients in quinary nanoparticles are an order of magnitude lower than in binary alloys
